dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi Priya, yes, hello. Siobhan Dolan here. I'm calling about my water and sewer bill. It came in yesterday and it's about double what I normally pay, and I honestly can't figure out why.
Okay, I can look at that with you. What's the service address?
260 Ocean Avenue. Over on the Ocean Drive side.
Thank you. And the name on the account is Dolan?

Dolan, yes. D-O-L-A-N. Sorry, one second, I'm sorting the mail here, I let it pile up on the table. Okay. That's the gas company, that's a flyer, that's, um, the dentist, that's another flyer. Sorry. Go ahead.
No problem. I have the account up. The most recent bill shows a usage figure that's roughly twice the previous quarter's. Does that match the bill you have in front of you?

Let me find it. It's in one of these piles. Library notice, no. Something from the insurance people, no. Oh, here, it's the one with the window. City of Newport, Water Division. Yes. Okay, so it says, um, well, it's a lot more than last time. It's almost exactly double.
Right, that's what I'm seeing too. Has anything changed at the house? More people staying, a new appliance, any irrigation or a pool?

No, nothing like that. Same as always. It's just me. Oh, wait, actually, the toilet. The toilet in the upstairs bathroom was running constantly last month. You'd flush it and it would just keep going, that hissing sound. I jiggled the handle for weeks. Then I finally replaced the flapper thing, I think that's what it's called.
That could well account for it. A running toilet can use a surprising amount of water without anyone noticing, and it shows up on the meter the whole time. When did you fix it?
Um, the end of last month. Maybe the twenty-fifth or so. So it ran for, I don't know, most of the month before that.
Sorry, this is the electric bill, hang on. No, that's not even mine, that's for the neighbor. I'll walk it over later. Okay, I'm back.
That's fine. So the usage on this bill would cover the period when it was running. Do you want to know how the charge was calculated, or are you looking to dispute it?
I'd like to dispute it, I think. How do I do that formally? Is there a form, or do I write a letter, or what?

You'd submit a written request to the water division asking for a review of the bill. Include your name, the service address, the account number, the bill date, and a short explanation. In your case, mention the running toilet and the date you repaired it. If you have a receipt for the part, attach a copy.
I do have the receipt, I think. It's in the, well, it's in one of these piles probably. Hardware store receipt. I'll find it. Do I mail it, or bring it in?
Either works. You can mail it to the utilities office at City Hall or drop it off at the counter during business hours. I'd suggest keeping a copy for yourself.
Okay. And what happens after that? Do they just take off the extra?

Not automatically. They review the request, and sometimes they check the meter readings. Whether any adjustment is made, and how much, is decided by that review. I can't tell you the result in advance.
That's fair. Should I pay it in the meantime?

I'd have to confirm how a pending review affects the due date. Let me put a note on the account that you're calling about it, and I'll check with my supervisor on that point. Can I reach you at a number?
Sure. It's 401-555-0155. That's my cell. I may not pick up if I'm out, but leave a message.
Got it, 401-555-0155. I'll note it. Is that the best time of day to call, around midday?

Midday's fine. Or the afternoon. Oh, here's the receipt, I found it. It was under the, hold on, the Christmas card from my cousin. Okay, so it's dated the twenty-sixth. So I fixed it the twenty-sixth, not the twenty-fifth.
Good, then put the twenty-sixth in your letter. That's the kind of specific detail that helps.
Okay. Twenty-sixth. And I should say the toilet was running the whole month before that?
Say what you actually observed. If you noticed it running for a few weeks, say a few weeks. Keep it accurate.
Okay, that makes sense. A few weeks. Alright. I think that's everything. Do I need the account number from you?
It should be printed near the top of your bill, on the right side. Take a look.
Let me see. Yes, got it, right there at the top. Great.
Perfect. Then you're set to write the request. I'll add the note and follow up with you about the due date.
Thank you, Priya. That was really clear. I appreciate it.
You're welcome, Ms. Dolan. Have a good afternoon.
You too. Bye now.
